## Classes and first visit

Fridays, 7:00pm – 9:00pm. Aylestone Leisure Centre, 2 Knighton Lane East, Leicester, LE2 6LU. First introductory lesson free. Advance booking is not required for the introductory class.

The home page shows the next class in Europe/London time, including confirmed cancellations or changed hours. Check the home page before travelling.

Class exception dated 2027-06-25: 18:00–20:00 (Europe/London).

Class exception dated 2027-10-01: 18:00–20:00 (Europe/London).

Children aged 12 and under may train only if their parent is also training. Please contact the instructor before bringing a child to confirm age eligibility and availability.

Wear loose-fitting exercise clothes that cover your knees. Avoid shorts, as practice includes kneeling.

Adult (waged): £25 monthly training; £35 separate annual UK Aikikai membership, including liability insurance.

Adult (concession): £20 monthly training; £27 separate annual UK Aikikai membership, including liability insurance.

Under 18: £15 monthly training; £20 separate annual UK Aikikai membership, including liability insurance.

Guest session: £8. Ask the instructor about registration, insurance cover and payment.

Contact: https://leicesteraikikai.com/contact. Sending an enquiry does not reserve a class place. The form requires Netlify Forms to be enabled on the deployed site.

## Club

Founded May 2013. Chief instructor and founder: Antonios Pavlakis, 4th Dan · Fukushidoin. United Kingdom Aikikai affiliation.

### Current instructor qualifications and certifications

- 4th Dan (Yondan) (2023)

- Fukushidoin (Teaching Qualification) (2018)

- JAC Coaching Level 3 (2022)

- DBS (Enhanced) (2026)

## Beginner questions

### Do I need previous martial arts experience?

No. Complete beginners are welcome, as are people returning to training. You can start with the fundamentals.

### What should I wear?

Wear loose-fitting exercise clothes that cover your knees. Avoid shorts, as practice includes kneeling.

### Do I need to be physically fit?

You do not need to reach a particular level of fitness before getting in touch. We welcome different levels of fitness and experience. Talk to the instructor about your needs before taking part.

### Is there a minimum age?

Children aged 12 and under may train only if their parent is also training. Please contact the instructor before bringing a child to confirm age eligibility and availability.

### What happens during my first class?

Meet the instructor and let them know you are new. Aikido practice includes partner movement, throws and learning how to fall and roll. The instructor can explain how you will begin; the exact lesson content varies.

### How much does training cost?

Your first introductory lesson is free. Monthly training is £25 for adult (waged), £20 for adult (concession), £15 for under 18. Separate annual UK Aikikai membership fees apply if you continue.

### Do I need to book in advance?

The club invites newcomers to come along on a Friday; advance booking is not required for the introductory class. You are welcome to contact us first with questions. Please enquire before bringing a child.

## Blog articles — original publication context

### Leicester Aikikai Aikido guest instructors July 2026

URL: https://leicesteraikikai.com/blog/2026-06-14/leicester-aikikai-aikido-guest-instructors-july-2026

Published: 14.06.2026. Updated: 14.06.2026. Author: Antonis Pavlakis.

In July 2026, Leicester Aikikai will welcome guest instructors from British Aikikai, British Birankai, and United Kingdom Aikikai for Friday night training sessions in the build-up to the UKA Summer School.

In July 2026, in the build-up to the United Kingdom Aikikai Summer School, we will invite guest instructors to join us and teach alongside me. Following last year’s success, we are looking forward to sharing the mat with new and familiar faces once again.

#### A shared summer training tradition

Guest instruction has become one of the best parts of our summer training calendar. It gives everyone a chance to experience different teaching styles, different approaches to movement, and a fresh atmosphere on the mat while staying grounded in traditional Aikikai practice.

Last year’s guest instructor sessions were a success, and they showed how much can be gained when local dojo and visiting teachers come together in one place.

#### Confirmed instructors for July 2026

So far, we have confirmations from instructors from British Aikikai, British Birankai, and United Kingdom Aikikai. That mix of backgrounds should make for lively and valuable training sessions, with each guest bringing their own perspective to the mat.

As more details are confirmed, we will continue to share the plan with the dojo so everyone knows what to expect from the July sessions.

#### Training Aikido in Leicester

If you are training aikido in Leicester, guest instructor evenings are a great way to stay motivated and expand your understanding of the art. They also offer a chance to meet other practitioners, exchange ideas, and keep your training fresh.

We hold our Friday night classes at 7pm, and if you want to join us you are always welcome to drop by and take part.

July 2026 should be another exciting month of training at Leicester Aikikai. We are grateful to the guest instructors who will join us, and we look forward to welcoming everyone onto the mat.

Join us on a Friday night: If you want to join us, drop by on a Friday night at 7pm and take part in the class. https://leicesteraikikai.com/#location
